conclusions: Exhaustive finite index oracle, missed-alternate candidate witness, empty-Jaccard failure and finite publication success/failures retained from incremental reports. No real corpus precision/recall or multiprocessing claim.

Original text conversion confirms documented whitespace/blank-line stripping and repeated-paragraph marking. Distinct file bytes normalize to identical unique paragraph fingerprints; deliberate text policy, not exact-file identity. Blank-only returnsNone, invalidUTF8raises.
utils/redisSimhash.py entirely commented code: no executable Redis index implementation. No Redis runtime test is required to interpret this file, and no Redis behavior is qualified.

Corpus extraction deletes source archive after reported success and extracted-size comparison; failed extraction may remove output directory based on path-length guard. No content integrity/ownership/expansion budget proven by source; extraction operations not executed.

Archive helper manually writes renamed long-name members and otherwise delegates extraction to format libraries. Path containment, archive bombs and external library semantics not qualified. No crafted archive exploitation or user data executed.

clean_file writes a removal-path list; despite wording in corpus readme it does not itself delete files. move_file and filename encoding script do move originals. These utilities differ from report-only library contract.
